title: Cleaning and Sanitising a Meat Processing System

lessons.title: Cleaning and sanitising: what is the difference
lessons.html:
Two different jobs

Cleaning removes dirt, blood, fat and meat scraps. Sanitising kills most of the germs that are left. You must clean first. A sanitiser does not work on a dirty surface, because fat and blood protect the germs.

Why it matters

  • Germs on tables, knives, saws and hooks spread to meat.
  • Dirty meat makes people sick and the abattoir can be closed.
  • Fat and blood left on floors make them slippery.
  • Leftover scraps bring flies and rats.

What you use

ItemWhat it does
WaterRinses off loose dirt. Must be clean drinking-quality water.
DetergentBreaks down fat and protein so it washes off.
SanitiserKills germs on a clean surface.
Brushes and scrapersRemove stuck dirt. Use the right colour brush for each area.
Hoses and pressure washersRinse large areas. Use low pressure near meat and equipment to avoid splashing.

Only approved chemicals

Use only the detergents and sanitisers that the abattoir has approved for food areas. Read the label and the safety data sheet. Mix them at the strength on the label. Too weak does not work. Too strong is dangerous, wastes money and can leave chemical on the meat.

Never mix two chemicals together. Some mixtures, such as chlorine with acid, give off poisonous gas.

lessons.title: The cleaning steps
lessons.html:
Follow the steps in order

Most abattoirs clean in the same order. Your cleaning schedule tells you what to clean, when, how and with what.

  1. Prepare: remove all meat and offal from the area. Switch off and lock out machines. Cover electrical boxes.
  2. Dry clean: scrape and pick up meat scraps, fat and bones. Put them in the right bins. Do not hose them into the drains.
  3. Pre-rinse: rinse with warm water from top to bottom. Hot water that is too hot can cook protein onto surfaces.
  4. Apply detergent: spray or brush the detergent on. Leave it for the contact time on the label.
  5. Scrub: scrub surfaces, corners, joints and under tables with brushes.
  6. Rinse: rinse off all detergent from top to bottom.
  7. Inspect: look and touch. The surface should be free of fat and dirt.
  8. Sanitise: apply the sanitiser at the right strength and leave it for the contact time on the label. Rinse after if the label says so.
  9. Dry and store: let equipment drain. Store small items off the floor.

Hard-to-clean places

  • Under and behind tables and conveyors.
  • Saw blades and guards.
  • Hooks, gambrels and rails.
  • Drains and drain covers.
  • Door handles, switches and hand basins.

Working from top to bottom

Always clean from high to low and from clean areas to dirty areas. Otherwise dirty water drips onto places you have already cleaned.

lessons.title: Working safely with cleaning chemicals
lessons.html:
Chemicals can hurt you

Cleaning chemicals can burn skin and eyes and damage your lungs. The Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 says your employer must give you training and protective equipment, and you must use it.

Protective equipment

  • Chemical-resistant gloves.
  • Goggles or a face shield.
  • Waterproof apron and gumboots.
  • A mask if the label says so.

Safe rules

  • Read the label before you use any chemical.
  • Keep chemicals in their own labelled containers. Never put them in cold drink bottles.
  • Add chemical to water, not water to chemical.
  • Never mix chemicals.
  • Store chemicals in a locked store away from meat and food.
  • Lock out machines before you clean them. Never put your hand into a moving machine.
  • Be careful on wet floors. Walk, do not run.

If there is an accident

  • Chemical in the eyes: rinse with lots of clean running water for a long time, at the eye wash station if there is one. Get help and show the label.
  • Chemical on skin: take off wet clothing and rinse the skin well with water.
  • Breathing in fumes: move to fresh air at once and tell your supervisor.

Report every accident. First aid must be given by a trained first aider. You need hands-on training from an accredited provider to give first aid.

Recording

Sign the cleaning record when you finish. Write the area, the time, the chemicals used and your name. The supervisor checks and signs before work starts.

Key points

  • Clean first, then sanitise. Sanitiser does not work on dirt.
  • Use only approved chemicals at the strength on the label.
  • Clean from top to bottom and from clean to dirty areas.
  • Never mix chemicals and always wear protective equipment.
  • Lock out machines before cleaning them.
